title: Extreme Environments Push Chips To Their Breaking Point
gist: Orbital data centers, defense systems, quantum, particle physics and advanced fabs are forcing chips to survive combined stresses (radiation, cryogenic cold, thermal shock, EMP), pushing demand for rad-hard designs at newer nodes and for multi-physics simulation plus physical test. Synopsys cites a major uptick in rad-hard fab-process activity, driven partly by Golden Dome.

themes.theme: Rad-hard demand from space and defense

insights.claim: Synopsys reports a major uptick in activity for rad-hard fab processes, particularly at new process nodes, to support orbital data centers.
insights.speaker: Dana Neustadter (Synopsys)
insights.so_what: Rad-hard EDA/IP and specialty foundry capacity at advanced nodes is an emerging demand pocket tied to space compute.
insights.locator: We have seen a major uptick

insights.claim: The Golden Dome multi-layered US missile defense initiative is a key driver of rad-hard design investment, on the premise that space is the next battlefield, and Synopsys expects many more rad-hard designs to be added.
insights.speaker: Dana Neustadter (Synopsys)
insights.so_what: Defense budget flows into space-grade silicon, a policy-backed demand leg beyond commercial AI.
insights.locator: A lot of this is owing to the Golden Dome

insights.claim: Growth in satellite constellations, orbital data centers, probes, surface explorers and military space systems is raising demand for radiation-hardened designs even at newer nodes, where performance and power gains must be traded against survivability.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Rad-hard no longer means only legacy nodes; the node-versus-survivability tradeoff creates design-service opportunity.
insights.locator: Space is becoming one of the clearest pressure points

insights.claim: Synopsys frames node migration as a mission-level decision: a hypothetical TSMC 1.5nm process promising 30% power savings would prompt re-spinning blocks for the next mission, validated through system-level simulation.
insights.speaker: Shawn Carpenter (Synopsys)
insights.so_what: Simulation-driven re-spin economics favor EDA vendors as space customers chase power efficiency.
insights.locator: If suddenly TSMC comes out

insights.claim: Governments are competing for leadership in emerging technologies, so space and extreme-environment electronics are treated as strategic beyond national security alone.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: State-backed funding supports a durable niche independent of commercial cycles.
insights.locator: Beyond national security

insights.claim: DARPA's Rads to Watts program, with PNNL, Morgan State University, Northrop Grumman and Project Omega, aims to convert radioactive decay into high-density radiovoltaic micro-power for space, remote sensing, undersea infrastructure and defense.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Radioisotope-plus-semiconductor power is an early-stage niche for power-semiconductor and materials players.
insights.locator: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL)

insights.claim: Rads to Watts converts isotopes such as Strontium-90 directly to electricity using ultra-thin semiconductor layers with beta-emitting isotopes, targeting decades of operation without refueling or battery replacement.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: If it scales, it removes battery limits for remote and undersea sensing.
insights.locator: Radioisotopes such as Strontium-90

insights.claim: Orbital data centers use sun-synchronous solar power for now, but nuclear micro reactors could later support deep-space propulsion, lunar and Martian bases and in-orbit manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Power remains the binding constraint for off-planet compute, which makes nuclear a possible long-dated enabler.
insights.locator: While orbital data centers are leveraging

insights.claim: Infineon's Helmut Puchner warns that a reactor accident in orbit would spread radioactive material that eventually falls toward the atmosphere over years to decades, and that more critical material in orbit means more risk on top of existing debris.
insights.speaker: Helmut Puchner (Infineon Technologies)
insights.so_what: Orbital nuclear power faces regulatory and public-acceptance risk that could slow deployment.
insights.locator: A nuclear reactor is basically

insights.claim: Chips once qualified against a limited set of operating conditions are now designed for environments where radiation, thermal shock, vibration, pressure, noise and cryogenic temperatures hit at once, so reliability can no longer be a final qualification step.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Reliability shifts left into design, raising value for simulation and test tooling.
insights.locator: Chips that were once qualified

insights.claim: Backside power delivery is breaking the laser-assisted device alteration (LADA) wafer-analysis technique because power on the backside blocks light, pushing fabs to consider X-ray-assisted device alteration (XADA), which risks X-ray damage to the material.
insights.speaker: Hugh Barnaby (ASU)
insights.so_what: Backside power adoption creates a failure-analysis tooling gap, which opens a market for new debug and test equipment.
insights.locator: in semiconductor manufacturing, lithography causes radiation damage

insights.claim: Semiconductors behave strangely at very low temperatures and more so when radiation is combined with cold; ASU modeling and theory are still being developed.
insights.speaker: Hugh Barnaby (ASU)
insights.so_what: Cryogenic-plus-radiation physics is immature, a risk for quantum and space designs and a research opportunity.
insights.locator: Barnaby and one of his students

insights.claim: ASU's Rigel DSTAT lab tool uses three rods holding 9,000 Curies of radioactive material plus a cryostat to test devices for radiation at 77 Kelvin using liquid nitrogen or argon.
insights.speaker: Hugh Barnaby (ASU)
insights.so_what: Combined-stress test capacity is scarce and bespoke, a bottleneck for space and quantum qualification.
insights.locator: Lab tools are evolving

insights.claim: Random telegraph noise has emerged as one of the biggest reliability problems, especially in analog and mixed-signal electronics, and it does not improve at best with cold in CMOS readout circuits even though cold helps the detector diodes.
insights.speaker: Hugh Barnaby (ASU)
insights.so_what: Cold readout ICs for satellites and quantum sensors face unresolved noise limits that cap performance gains.
insights.quote: random telegraph noise has emerged as one of the biggest reliability problems today, especially in analog/mixed-signal electronics.
insights.locator: The tool was ideal

insights.claim: ASU's extreme-environment lab is extending into advanced packaging reliability (pressure, humidity, high temperature, thermal and mechanical shock, vibration) and works with NXP at its Phoenix facility.
insights.speaker: Hugh Barnaby (ASU)
insights.so_what: Extreme-environment test methods are spilling into mainstream advanced packaging qualification.
insights.locator: The applications for these kinds of lab tools

insights.claim: Particle accelerators, proton-therapy equipment and X-ray-using fabs face extremely high radiation doses where equipment must function while being damaged.
insights.speaker: Hugh Barnaby (ASU)
insights.so_what: Radiation-tolerant electronics demand extends to medical and science markets, not just space.
insights.locator: Particle accelerators and research accelerators

themes.theme: Simulation, digital twins and AI in design

insights.claim: AI-enabled tools, ML and language models can explore more design options earlier, but virtual models must still be checked against physical behavior because the challenge is reproducing enough of the real environment to trust predictions.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: AI in EDA complements rather than replaces physical test, so test and lab-tool vendors keep their relevance.
insights.locator: That is changing how chips are designed

insights.claim: Fermilab and Siemens are running AXESS, using LLMs and smaller surrogate models to speed design exploration and co-optimize all chip development stages for quantum computing, fusion energy and particle physics.
insights.speaker: Liz Allan
insights.so_what: Siemens is positioning LLM-driven EDA at DOE labs for extreme-environment chips.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, the U.S. Department of Energy

insights.claim: A 4D geospatial model and digital twin carrying thermal and radiation data lets engineers predict how components stretch, shrink and stress, which matters for the extreme swings from direct sun to shadow in space.
insights.speaker: Shawn Carpenter (Synopsys)
insights.so_what: Multi-physics digital twins are a growth area for EDA and simulation vendors in space programs.
insights.locator: Simulating electronics for space

insights.claim: Thermal cycling in space can range from -40F to 120F in a single day, which shortens electronics lifetime, and radiation from solar particles in transistor oxides further degrades performance.
insights.speaker: Lang Lin (Synopsys)
insights.so_what: Space lifetime is limited by thermal cycling and oxide damage, so process choice and packaging matter more than raw node.
insights.locator: Another stressor is that, in outer space

insights.claim: Synopsys sells IP and simulation to shorten the time to build a space chipset, modeling heat, signal integrity, aging and lifetime from chip to package to carrier board to module.
insights.speaker: Shawn Carpenter (Synopsys)
insights.so_what: System-level modeling is the monetization path for EDA vendors in extreme-environment design.
insights.locator: Designers need to build chips

insights.claim: Positional data for objects in orbit or on the lunar surface must be protected against spoofing in digital-twin and AI systems.
insights.speaker: Dana Neustadter (Synopsys)
insights.so_what: Space data security is a parallel demand driver for security IP.
insights.locator: Simulation, digital twinning, and AI-enabled tools

insights.claim: Military space vehicles are expected to become mobile, reactive, drone-like and armed, which Synopsys expects to require agentic AI that is mostly autonomous and learns.
insights.speaker: Dana Neustadter (Synopsys)
insights.so_what: Edge autonomy in space is a speculative demand vector for onboard AI silicon.
insights.locator: Agentic AI will also be part of the equation

insights.claim: Because communication costs are high at the desired data rates, space systems benefit from processing locally and sending back only critical information.
insights.speaker: Dana Neustadter (Synopsys)
insights.so_what: Bandwidth constraints make onboard inference the logical design point for orbital compute.
insights.locator: AI doesn't always enhance safety

insights.claim: Space electronics need EMP and high-altitude EMP protection from nuclear events or solar storms, which means shielding and grounding that are expensive and not required in commercial aviation (DO-160 EMC).
insights.speaker: Lang Lin (Synopsys)
insights.so_what: Shielding adds cost to defense and space hardware beyond the silicon itself.
insights.locator: Counteracting radiation

insights.claim: No terrestrial data centers have EMP protection today, but space-based ones will likely need specialized shielding, which would raise orbital data center development costs.
insights.speaker: Lang Lin (Synopsys)
insights.so_what: Orbital data center economics carry a cost penalty versus ground-based compute.
insights.quote: Currently, no data centers here on Earth have EMP protection, but space-based ones will likely need specialized shielding, which would raise development costs for orbital data centers.
insights.locator: Then you're going to have to replace it

insights.claim: Cosmic-ray bit flips can be catastrophic for AI training runs and inference; mitigation uses voting across multiple GPUs and in-GPU checks borrowed from automotive functional safety.
insights.speaker: Matthew Bubis (Imagination Technologies)
insights.so_what: Automotive-grade safety IP carries over to space and large AI clusters, widening its market.
insights.locator: On Earth, AI data centers and automotive

insights.claim: In space, bit flips pose a reliability problem rather than a safety problem, and survivability is multi-layered: the chipmaker handles radiation hardening and others add protection around the chip.
insights.speaker: Matthew Bubis (Imagination Technologies)
insights.so_what: Value is spread across foundry, IP and system-level shielding, not captured by one layer.
insights.locator: Many automotive-grade safety features
